ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Voltaire Synthetic CCD — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

text.paragraph: Primary care visit for three weeks of visible blood in the urine and difficult urination at 83. Concerns: Blood in the urine and difficulty passing water for three weeks; afraid it is something serious; Wants to finish the play he is staging and to keep writing, and does not want long stays in hospital; Has always taken many remedies of his own choosing and asks for something strong to make him sleep. [S]

Tamsulosin 0.4 mg oral capsule, one capsule at bedtime
One capsule 30 minutes after the evening meal
Polyethylene glycol 3350, 17 g in a glass of water once daily
17 g dissolved in water once daily
Cefpodoxime 200 mg oral tablet, one tablet by mouth twice daily for 7 days
One tablet twice daily with food for 7 days
Acetaminophen 500 mg oral tablet, two tablets by mouth three times daily (3 g a day)
Two tablets three times daily; no more than 3 g a day
Oxycodone 5 mg oral tablet, one half tablet (2.5 mg) by mouth every 6 hours if needed for bladder pain not relieved by acetaminophen, no more than three doses a day; 15 tablets dispensed

Naloxone 4 mg nasal spray, one spray in one nostril for suspected opioid overdose; call 911; may repeat in 2 to 3 minutes in the other nostril
One spray for suspected overdose; repeat after 2 to 3 minutes if no response

tr.td: Insertion of a 16 Fr two-way indwelling urethral catheter in the clinic: 520 mL of pink urine drained without clots

Multiphasic CT urography: 4.2 cm sessile soft-tissue mass of the posterior bladder wall extending to the dome, with wall thickening to 1.8 cm and perivesical fat stranding (suspected extravesical extension); no hydronephrosis; upper tracts clear; prostate about 78 mL with a median lobe; no enlarged pelvic or retroperitoneal nodes; no bone lesions
CT of the chest with contrast, done with the urography: no lung nodule, mass, or mediastinal lymph node; airways clear; no source for the earlier bleeding from the mouth

Flexible cystoscopy by urology: solid, sessile, partly necrotic tumor about 4 cm on the posterior wall extending to the dome, with surrounding white keratinizing plaques; trilobar prostatic enlargement with friable surface vessels; catheter replaced

Transurethral resection of the bladder tumor with examination under anesthesia: a mobile, palpable mass (cT3b); resection to muscle. Pathology: keratinizing squamous cell carcinoma, moderately differentiated, invading the muscularis propria, with lymphovascular invasion; no urothelial carcinoma component and no carcinoma in situ; catheter left for drainage
Change of the urethral catheter at the sick visit, with a urine culture from the new catheter
Trial without catheter on tamsulosin: voided 260 mL with a post-void residual of 140 mL
CT of the bladder for radiotherapy planning
Hypofractionated external beam radiotherapy to the bladder, 36 Gy in six weekly fractions of 6 Gy, with daily image guidance, by the radiation oncology team; fractions 1 and 2 given by the last visit

tr.td: Visible blood in the urine for three weeks with clots, and a weak stream, straining, and frequent small voids, in a man of 83; under evaluation
S — Synthetic presenting problem echoing his documented urinary complaints and last illness; superseded by the diagnosis at the third chronic-care visit.
Chronic urinary retention with overflow (post-void residual 460 mL at intake), worsened by a nightly anticholinergic sleep aid; drained by an indwelling catheter
S — Synthetic finding echoing the strangury and catheterization documented in his last weeks.
Acute kidney injury from bladder outlet obstruction (creatinine 1.68 mg/dL, from 1.1 mg/dL a year earlier)
S — Synthetic finding; it echoes, without asserting, the later encyclopedia term uremia.

Benign prostatic hyperplasia with lower urinary tract symptoms: prostate about 78 mL on CT, enlarged, firm, and smooth on examination, PSA 6.4 ng/mL with a PSA density of 0.08; no prostate biopsy, by shared decision
S — Synthetic diagnosis echoing the very large prostate described at the 1778 autopsy; whether that prostate was malignant is unknown (CLM-0012).

Squamous cell carcinoma of the bladder, keratinizing, posterior wall extending to the dome, muscle-invasive with extravesical extension (clinical stage cT3b N0 M0, stage IIIA), pure squamous histology without a urothelial component; treated with palliative-intent hypofractionated radiotherapy by shared decision

S — Synthetic modern diagnosis confirmed by resection pathology. His bladder disease at autopsy is documented (D); calling it squamous cell carcinoma is a 2025 retrospective interpretation (R, disputed).
Chronic constipation, lifelong by his account, with long use of laxatives and self-given enemas
S — Synthetic modern problem echoing his documented colic, purges, and enemas; no diagnosis of inflammatory bowel disease is made.
Febrile catheter-associated urinary tract infection with Escherichia coli, five days after bladder tumor resection; treated with cefpodoxime and a catheter change; resolved
S — Synthetic intercurrent infection; it echoes, without asserting, the infected urine described in his last weeks (CLM-0009).

tr.td: Primary care visit for three weeks of visible blood in the urine and difficult urination at 83
One-week review of CT urography and kidney function; urology consultation with office cystoscopy
Review of resection pathology, diagnosis, geriatric assessment, trial without catheter, and shared decision on treatment
Two-week review during weekly radiotherapy: symptoms, kidney function, voiding, and opioid safety
Same-day sick visit for fever with a catheter after bladder tumor resection
Hematuria evaluation: urinalysis with microscopy, urine culture, urine cytology, blood count, kidney function, multiphasic CT urography with CT of the chest, and cystoscopy
Urology consultation for gross hematuria with chronic retention: cystoscopy, resection if a tumor is found, the voiding trial, and the meaning of the PSA
Retention: indwelling catheter now, tamsulosin at bedtime, catheter care teaching, then a trial without catheter with a bladder scan; IPSS and post-void residual at each visit

Medication review: stop the diphenhydramine sleep aid and the over-the-counter sodium phosphate enemas; keep polyethylene glycol; cut coffee to two cups a day, none after noon; sleep advice without sedatives

Shared decision on PSA testing: drawn before the catheter to interpret an enlarged, firm prostate, with the understanding that a raised value at 83 would lead to biopsy only if it would change treatment
Transurethral resection of the bladder tumor with examination under anesthesia, for diagnosis and staging
Geriatric assessment (G8 screen, function, falls, cognition, mood, nutrition, social support, and medicines) before choosing cancer treatment

Shared decision on treatment of muscle-invasive squamous cell carcinoma: radical cystectomy, trimodality bladder preservation, palliative hypofractionated radiotherapy, or symptom care alone; he chose weekly radiotherapy, 36 Gy in six fractions, given by the radiation oncology team

Pain plan: scheduled acetaminophen; oxycodone 2.5 mg only if needed, no more than three doses a day, 15 tablets at a time from one prescriber; naloxone nasal spray; senna; the state prescription monitoring program checked; no alcohol, sleep aids, or anyone else's opium-based remedies; doses kept in a locked box; review within two weeks
Palliative care team joins his care alongside radiotherapy for symptom control, goals of care, and support at home
Advance care planning: name a health care agent and complete a portable medical order reflecting his wishes
Find the cause of the bleeding within three weeks
CT urography in two days, cystoscopy in one week, resection in nine days; pathology reviewed at sixteen days
Relieve the retention and recover kidney function
Creatinine 1.68 to 1.22 mg/dL; voiding after the trial without catheter with a residual of 140 mL
Treatment that controls bleeding and local symptoms while keeping him at home and writing
Weekly radiotherapy under way; no clots or retention since the resection; writing most days
Pain at or below 3 of 10 without sedation, falls, or constipation
Pain 2 of 10 on scheduled acetaminophen and about one half tablet of oxycodone a day; no sedation
A written plan for future care, with a named health care agent
Health care agent named and a portable medical order completed at the wellness visit
